translation.english_title: Hey, do not be lost in a dream

source_tamil_lines: நீ வாராய் ராஜா... நீ வாராய் ராஜா...
english_lines: Hey, do not be lost in a dream,
Think so — one day, embrace me,
Both eyes are little, little flowers,
O man whose hands seek a woman's body,
You have done it to the word,
O season that came seeking the alli flower,
Think so — one day, embrace me,
notes: `குறமுல்லை` is retained as `Kuramullai` because the verified anthology form does not support a safe replacement.
`சொல்லுக்கு செய்தாயே` is kept deliberately close to the source as `You have done it to the word`; the English does not invent a missing object or action.
`பாட்டுப்பட்ட` is represented conservatively as `song-struck`, retaining the source compound instead of substituting a familiar soundtrack wording.

source_tamil_lines: ரம்மை போல கண்ணு ஜின்னை போல கண்ணும்
ஜாடை ஒன்று காட்டி நாடி வரும் நாட்டி
english_lines: To those who come, he pours out and gives,
He came as though a vallal had arrived in person,
An eye like rammai, and an eye like jinnai too,
Showing one gesture — the naatti who comes seeking,
I myself came seeking you and stood here,
Think so — one day, embrace me,
notes: `வள்ளல்` remains `vallal`, preserving the culturally loaded generous-patron image.
The verified source sequence `ரம்மை போல கண்ணு ஜின்னை போல கண்ணும்` is not repaired from soundtrack familiarity; `rammai` and `jinnai` remain transliterated pressure points.
`நாடி வரும் நாட்டி` is retained conservatively with `naatti` rather than assigning an unsupported identity or profession.

translator_notes: The song mixes flirtation with colloquial, source-anomalous phrases. The English preserves those pressures rather than rewriting them into smoother romantic lyric prose.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
